intro: Every day the dice roll a premise and a dozen constraints, and the game has to honor all of them. Today's roll was seed 1835081946. Here is each roll and what came of it, darling.

rolls.became: Why would a bookworm decorate its teeth? Because old books have real gold on their spines. Gold leaf is gold beaten so thin it sticks to whatever bites it, so a worm that eats titles ends up with gilded teeth. Quarto just does it on purpose.

One tap, three meanings. By night it's a bite out of the gilt title on the spine; by day it's a whisper through the pages; in the rare-books room, where chewing sets off the alarm, it's a smile at the fans.

The Spine, the worms' gossip page, only ever writes about one grin: Isadora's. She lives in the Illuminated Psalter in the glass case and got her gold teeth eating its gold-leaf capitals. The meter is your grin against hers.

Worms have no money, and gold leaf is about four hundred atoms thick. A bite is trillions of atoms and weighs nothing at all: the game counts your gold in atoms and then, cruelly, in grams. And the bottom shelf only has foil.
Isadora, and the great illuminated I in her Psalter, where her gold came from.
Numbers in atoms: trillions a bite, quadrillions on the encyclopedia shelf, sextillions by the end. The whole library's gilt, every letter of every title, comes to about two grams.

rolls.value: limited space to arrange (a grid, shelf or map)
rolls.became: The grid is Quarto's mouth: sixteen teeth, and only the four front ones show on the bottom shelf. Every shelf adds one rule. Matching foil side by side shines; gold caps in a row make a grill; a gem set under a gold cap counts double. So the studs you couldn't resist on the encyclopedia shelf come back to haunt you.

rolls.value: distinct phases, each its own small economy
rolls.became: Three shelves, three currencies. Foil from the paperbacks, paid for with silverfish rent. Real gold leaf from the encyclopedias, with deathwatch beetles and cousins in reading glasses. Then pigment from fans in the rare-books room, traded for signed headshots.

Library hours. Closed at night, so the worms come out and chew. Open by day, so everyone hides in a book and gossips through the pages. At closing time the day's gossip turns into new cousins (later, fans) who chew for you.
There's no last button. The library only has so much gold leaf, and once everyone's chewing it, it runs out by itself.

Mabel borrows one fleck “just to see”. Folio learns to gild and teaches six cousins before lunch. Beat Isadora and her fans want gold grins too, then the silverfish, then Large Print. By dawn every title in the building is gone and the dark between the books is full of tiny gold grins.

A gold grin is the brightest thing in a dark library, so everything is drawn as glowing tube on a purple wall: the spines, the CLOSED sign, Quarto's glasses. When the lights come on by day, the neon dims.
Five tubes and a wall: pale gold for gilt, mint for Quarto, pink for lips and gossip, thistle for foil and teeth, and the purple, deepened, for the night.

A wind-up music box playing a slightly sly lullaby in D dorian, slow and rocking, in three. It fills out shelf by shelf, speeds up a little when everyone joins in, and slows right down for dawn. Every nibble and chime is on the same mode.
The log is The Spine, and Madame Marginalia rates every grin out of five. Volume IV is FURIOUS. Gaps are OUT. Write that down. Somewhere with a margin.

outro: Put all that together and you get a worm with a tiny budget, a famous rival and sixteen teeth to fill, who sets off a craze nobody can stop. Not even the library.
